_comment: CheXpert v1.0 (Stanford). Only the required keys and expected_stats are written here. The other config fields are not written yet.

expected_stats._comment: Checked by tests/test_dataset_stats.py, with the default drop_uncertain=True. Sources: the CheXpert paper (Irvin et al., AAAI 2019: 224,316 images of 65,240 patients, and a hidden test set of 500 patients), and train.csv and valid.csv read with pandas. Train + valid have 64,540 + 200 patients, plus 500 test patients = 65,240, as in the paper. Policy (wiki page): a blank label is 0, and a row with any -1 label is dropped. A row with every label blank has no label at all, so it gets NaN in every label (D-05, V-H1-41). uncertain counts these rows, from the raw label file read with pandas. All other rows stay, laterals too. valid.csv has no -1. Sex is Male, Female or Unknown in the source (D-26: M, F or NaN). 1 train row has Sex Unknown. Some train ages are 0.
